status: DRAFT answer key: written with the corpus, to be reviewed and signed off by the author before scoring.

must_find.why: The practice (custodian) is established in Subregion A1, a Subregion (Annex I).
Art 8(2)(c) health-care condition on the basis of Subregion law: A1-HIA 4(1) registered practitioners; A1-HIA 4(2) the agent acting on documented instructions is under their responsibility.
6(1)(b) contract: patients pay under terms of care. 6(1)(f) legitimate interests is unavailable for sensitive information (6(2)).
Signed agreement covers the 9(2) terms; its deletion term interacts with B-HRA 9 (see conflicts).

routes.A-REG 17 recognition: ruled_out: Annex II recognition of Region B extends only to non-sensitive information, despite the active certificate
routes.A-REG 18 approved clauses: unmet as described: clauses executed, but no 18(2) assessment, and Region B law (B-RAA 3, 4, 6) allows secret production orders without court authorisation; with Northgate holding the keys no effective supplementary measure exists, so 18(3) bars the transfer
routes.A-REG 19 derogations: ruled_out: the transfer is ongoing, so 19(1)(a)-(b) are excluded by 19(2); (c) and (d) do not fit

must_find.cure: Keep the decryption keys only within Region A (B-RAA 5 then removes the compelled-decryption risk), document the 18(2) assessment, and stop Northgate engineers in Region B opening plaintext records (support without key access, or practice-mediated).

must_find.why: Cumulative Subregion A1 condition (Art 8(3)): 30 days' prior notification to the Commission (not done) and Region A-held keys (keys are held by Northgate in Region B).

3,200 patients is below the 5,000 threshold in A-REG 12(2)(a), but A1-HIA 8(a) requires an assessment for hosting a patient record system outside Subregion A1 regardless of numbers; none was prepared.
Notice names the third territory and the route relied on.
Northgate is a data host; it must keep records 7 years unless it returns records that originated outside Region B and keeps no copy (9(2)). The agreement says delete within 30 days.
The practice bills no Region B insurer, so it is not a covered provider and Northgate is not its service agent (B-HRA 3(2)); B-HRA 4-8 do not apply.

conflicts.resolution: The custodian chooses return rather than deletion under A-REG 9(2)(f); returning records that originated outside Region B and keeping no copy satisfies B-HRA 9(2).

cross_jurisdiction.about: Public-authority access in Region B for the A-REG 18(2) assessment

must_not: Treat the Region B Trusted Recipient Scheme certificate as a valid Article 17 route for health records.
Require an impact assessment only because of A-REG 12(2)(a) numbers (3,200 < 5,000), or skip it because of them.
Rely on Article 19(1)(a) consent or 19(1)(b) contract for an ongoing hosting arrangement.
Rely on Article 6(1)(f) legitimate interests for health records.
Apply B-HRA 4-8 to the practice or to Northgate.
Treat a child-consent age rule (A-REG 7(2), A1-HIA 9) as engaged: no ground relies on consent.
